_comment: S19. One entry per acceptance test. Only `passes` may be flipped; never reword an entry.

features.description: Part A. An ungated call in the same reply as a gated one does not run before the person is asked.
Part A. The order the model put the calls in decides nothing: the whole batch is classified before any of it runs.
Part A. A held-back call executes on resume, in its original order, after the answers are in.
Part A. A denial holds back the calls nobody was asked about too, and tells the model they did not run.
Part A. A question a tool returns is not an approval: its neighbours still run, as upstream pins.
Part A. A turn with no approval in it is unchanged: same calls, same order, same number of model calls.
Part A. A pending call the person actually answered still records that answer as its result.
Part A. An answer for a call no question was raised for executes nothing and is never echoed back to the model.
Part A. A tool's own question left unanswered does not run that tool a second time.
Part A. The streamed loop holds back the same calls, opens no card for them, and leaves none spinning.
Part A. The pause and answer shapes the web apps read are unchanged.
Part B. An unattended run refuses a gated tool: it does not run and does not pause.
Part B. auto_approve alone still counts as unattended, so no existing caller changes meaning.
Part B. An unattended run still executes an ungated tool.
Part B. An attended run is unaffected: a gated tool still pauses and asks.
Part B. A trigger with auto_approve off refuses instead of parking the run in Paused, as the user it runs as.
Part B. A resume is never unattended: an approved gated call still executes.
Part B. The refusal text names no platform, vendor or model, and the check that says so can itself go red.
Part B. Only the _invoke digest moved; the other three load-bearing functions are byte-identical.
